    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">Many
      of
      these companies compete principally on the basis of price and may have lower
      costs than us, which allow them to offer the same products and services at
      lower
      prices.&#160;&#160;Many of our competitors are larger, have substantially
      greater financial, technical, marketing and other resources and offer a broader
      range of value-added services than we do.&#160;&#160;We compete with, among
      others, CompuCom Systems, Inc., Dell, Gateway, Pomeroy IT Solutions, Inc.,
      CDW
      Corporation, IBM, HP, Insight Enterprises, Inc., PC Mall, Inc., GTSI Corp.,
      Zones, Inc., PC Connection, Inc., and certain distributors.&#160;&#160;We expect
      to face additional competition from new market entrants in the
      future.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">Competitive
      factors include price, service and support, the variety of products and
      value-added services offered, and marketing and sales
      capabilities.&#160;&#160;While we believe that we compete successfully with
      respect to most, if not all of these factors, there can be no assurance that
      we
      will continue to do so in the future.&#160;&#160;The information technology
      industry has come to be characterized by aggressive price-cutting and we expect
      pricing pressures will continue in the foreseeable future.&#160;&#160;In
      addition, the information technology products industry is characterized by
      abrupt changes in technology and associated inventory and product obsolescence,
      rapid changes in consumer preferences, short product life cycles and evolving
      industry standards.&#160;&#160;We will need to continue to provide competitive
      prices, superior product selection and quick delivery response time in addition
      to developing a core competency in performing value-added services in order
      to
      remain competitive.&#160;&#160;If we were to fail to compete favorably with
      respect to any of these factors, our business, financial position, results
      of
      operations and cash flows would be materially and adversely
      affected.&#160;&#160;See &#8216;&#8216;Business&#8212;Competition.&#8217;&#8217;</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong>WE
      RISK DEPENDING ON A FEW DISTRIBUTORS AND MANUFACTURERS WHO COULD COMPETE WITH
      US
      OR LIMIT OUR ACCESS TO THEIR PRODUCT LINE</strong></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">A
      key
      element of our past success and future business strategy involves the
      maintaining of alliances with certain key suppliers of information technology
      products and services, including, Tech Data, Microsoft, Ingram Micro, Synnex,
      and Dell.&#160;&#160;These alliances enable us to make available to our
      customers a wide selection of products without subjecting us to many of the
      costs and risks associated with maintaining large amounts of
      inventory.&#160;&#160;Products and services purchased from those five suppliers,
      in fiscal years 2007, 2006 and 2005 accounted for 57%, 67%&#160;and 76% of our
      aggregate purchases.&#160;&#160;Furthermore, we compete with certain suppliers
      for many of the same customers.&#160;&#160;Therefore, there can be no assurance
      that any such allied distributor will not use its position as a key supplier
      to
      pressure us from directly competing with them.&#160;&#160;Substantially all of
      our contracts with our suppliers are terminable by either party upon 30 days
      notice or less and several contain minimum purchase volume requirements as
      a
      condition to providing discounts to us.&#160;&#160;The termination or
      interruption of our relationships with any of the suppliers, modification of
      the
      terms or discontinuance of agreements with any of the suppliers, failure to
      meet
      minimum purchase volume requirements, or the failure to maintain a good working
      relationship with any significant new distributor of information technology
      products could materially adversely affect our business, financial position,
      results of operations and cash flows.&#160;&#160;See &#8216;&#8216;Business&#8212;Getting Product
      to the Customer.&#8217;&#8217;</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">Certain
      of the products we offer are subject to manufacturer allocations, which limit
      the number of units of such products available to the suppliers, which in turn
      may limit the number of units available to us for resale to our
      customers.&#160;&#160;Because of these limitations, there can be no assurance
      that we will be able to offer popular new products or product enhancements
      to
      our customers in sufficient quantity or in a timely manner to meet
      demand.&#160;&#160;In order to offer the products of most manufacturers, we are
      required to obtain authorizations from such manufacturers to act as a reseller
      of such products, which authorizations may be terminated at the discretion
      of
      the suppliers.&#160;&#160;As well, certain manufacturers provide us with
      substantial incentives in the form of allowances, training, financing, rebates,
      discounts, credits and cooperative advertising, which incentives directly affect
      our operating income.&#160;&#160;There can be no assurance that we will continue
      to receive such incentives and authorizations in the future and any reduction
      in
      these incentives could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial
      position, results of operations and cash flows.&#160;&#160;There can also be no
      assurance that we will be able to obtain or maintain authorizations to offer
      products, directly or indirectly, from new or existing
      manufacturers.&#160;Termination of our rights to act as a reseller of the
      products of one or more significant manufacturers or our failure to gain
      sufficient access to such new products or product enhancements could have a
      material adverse effect on our business, financial position, results of
      operations and cash flows.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">Evolution
      of the distribution process in the information technology industry has put
      pressure on gross profit margins, and has adversely affected a number of
      distributors of information technology products, including certain
      suppliers.&#160;&#160;There can be no assurance that the continuing evolution of
      the information technology industry will not further adversely affect our
      distributors.&#160;&#160;Because our overall business strategy depends on our
      relationships with our suppliers, our business, financial position, results
      of
      operations and cash flows would be materially adversely affected in the event
      that distributors in general and suppliers in particular continue to suffer
      adverse consequences due to ongoing changes in the information technology
      industry.&#160;&#160;There has been a consolidation trend in the information
      technology industry, including consolidation among distributors of information
      technology products.&#160;&#160;Because our business model is dependent upon the

      Rancho Cucamonga, California also makes us more vulnerable to dramatic changes

      companies and which have often been unrelated to the operating performance
      of
      such companies.&#160;&#160;These broad market fluctuations may materially and
      adversely affect the market price of our common stock.&#160;&#160;See &#8216;&#8216;Market

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">Changing
      laws, regulations and standards relating to corporate governance and public
      disclosure, including the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 and related regulations
      implemented by the Securities and Exchange Commission, or SEC, and The Nasdaq
      Stock Market, or the Nasdaq, are creating uncertainty for public companies,
      increasing legal and financial compliance costs and making some activities
      more
      time consuming.&#160;&#160;We are undergoing an evaluation of our internal
      controls systems to allow management to report on, and our independent auditors
      to attest to, our internal controls.&#160;&#160;We are also in the process of
      performing the system and process evaluation and testing (and any necessary
      remediation) required to comply with the management certification and auditor
      attestation requirements of Section 404 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act.&#160;&#160;As
      a result, we expect to incur substantial additional expenses and diversion
      of
      management&#8217;s time.&#160;&#160;While we anticipate being able to fully implement
      the requirements relating to internal controls and all other aspects of Section
      404 by the extended September 30, 2008 deadline, we cannot be certain as to
      the
      timing of completion of our evaluation, testing and remediation actions or
      the
      impact of the same on our operations since there is presently no precedent
      available by which to measure compliance adequacy.&#160;&#160;If we are not able
      to implement the requirements of Section 404 in a timely manner or with adequate
      compliance, we may not be able to accurately report our financial results or
      prevent fraud and might be subject to sanctions or investigation by regulatory
      authorities, such as the SEC or the Nasdaq.&#160;&#160;Any such action could
      harm our business or investors&#8217; confidence in our company, and could cause our
      stock price to fall.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong>IF
      PREFERRED STOCK IS ISSUED AS AN ANTI-TAKEOVER MEASURE, THERE IS A RISK THAT
      THE
      PRICE OF OUR COMMON STOCK COULD BE ADVERSELY AFFECTED</strong></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">Our
      Board
      of Directors has the authority to issue up to 5,000,000 shares of preferred
      stock and to determine the price, rights,&#160;preferences, qualifications,
      limitations and restrictions, including voting rights, of those shares without
      any further vote or action by the stockholders.&#160;&#160;The rights of the
      holders of common stock will be subject to, and may be adversely affected by,
      the rights of the holders of any preferred stock that may be issued in the
      future.&#160;&#160;The issuance of preferred stock, while providing desirable
      flexibility in connection with possible acquisitions and other corporate
      purposes, could have the effect of delaying or preventing a third party from
      acquiring a majority of our outstanding voting stock.&#160;&#160;Further,
      Section 203 of the General Corporation Law of Delaware prohibits us from
      engaging in certain business combinations with interested
      stockholders.&#160;&#160;These provisions may have the effect of delaying or
      preventing a change in control of En Pointe without action by our stockholders,
      and therefore could adversely affect the market price of our common
      stock.</font></div>

      ARE RISKS OUTSIDE OF OUR CONTROL OF UNFAVORABLE ECONOMIC CONDITIONS THAT COULD
      NEGATIVELY IMPACT OUR REVENUES AND PROFITS</strong></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">Revenue
      growth depends on the overall demand for information technology
      spending.&#160;&#160;While economy in the United States appears to be stable,
      there can be no assurance that stability will continue.&#160;&#160;Any downturn
      in the United States&#8217; economy may result in cutbacks by customers in the
      purchase of information technology products and services, postponed or canceled
      orders, longer sales cycles and lower average selling prices.&#160;&#160;To the
      extent that a downturn occurs, we believe demand for our products and services,
      and therefore future revenues, could be further adversely impacted.</font></div>

      3,969 respectively.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">Management
      believes our headquarters, sales offices, configuration facility, and those
      offices of our affiliates&#160;are adequate to support our current level of
      operations.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong>ITEM
      3. <a name="legalProceedings">LEGAL PROCEEDINGS</a></strong></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">In
      July
      2006, Church&#160;Gardens, LLC, the current owner of our former leased
      configuration facility in Ontario, California, filed suit against us in San
      Bernardino County Superior Court, Case No. RCV096518. The complaint centers
      on
      certain furniture, fixtures, equipment and leasehold improvements that were
      sold
      to, and leased back from us, by plaintiff&#8217;s predecessor in 1999 when we still
      occupied our former leased configuration facility in Ontario, California. The
      plaintiff alleges, among other things, that a portion of the leased-back
      property was sold, destroyed, altered, or removed from the premises, and demands
      both an inspection and an accounting of the property remaining and for the
      court
      to provide damages to the extent that we may have breached our contract. We
      dispute the allegations and believe that any property loss liability under
      the
      lease provisions would be limited to the $75,000 that we have already accrued
      on
      our financial statements.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">In
      February 2007, we filed a cross-complaint against Church Gardens LLC. The
      cross-complaint asks that our $90,720 security deposit be returned with
      interest. In addition, we claim that Church Gardens LLC engaged in unfair
      business practices in retaining the security deposit and in not allowing the
      removal of certain personal property that we owned and that Church Gardens
      LLC
      engaged in unlawful conversion of certain property belonging to us. We also
      ask
      the court to grant declaratory relief as to our actions in our attempts to
      preserve the disputed property pending a judicial determination of rights.
      We
      also seek recovery of possession of our personal property and injunctive relief
      preventing the plaintiff from liquidating our property.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">In
      January 2007, US Real Estate Consortium, the predecessor owner of our former
      leased configuration facility in Ontario, California filed suit against the
      current owner, Church Gardens LLC, in San Bernardino County Superior Court,
      Case
      No. RCV100476.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">In
      March
      2007, the current owner, Church Gardens LLC, filed a cross-complaint against
      us
      and the former owner, US Real Estate Consortium, among others.&#160; On May 31,
      2007, we answered&#160;and cross-claimed against the current owner,
      Church&#160;Gardens, LLC. On July 25, 2007, Church&#160;Gardens, LLC filed its
      answer to the first amended cross-complaint filed by us.&#160; Both cases
      (RCV096518 and RCV100476) have now been consolidated for all
      purposes.&#160;</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">Although
      the first case (RCV096518) was originally filed in July 2006, no trial date
      in
      the now consolidated case has been set. There has been substantial discovery,
      and substantial law and motion practice to date. We are contesting the
      consolidated&#160;case vigorously, and intend to continue doing so.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">There
      are
      various other claims and litigation proceedings in which we are involved in
      the
      ordinary course of business.&#160;&#160;We accrue for costs related to
      contingencies when a loss is probable and the amount is reasonably
      determinable.&#160;&#160;While the outcome of the foregoing and other claims and
      proceedings cannot be predicted with certainty, after consulting with legal
      counsel, management does not believe that it is reasonably possible that any
      ongoing or pending litigation will result in an unfavorable outcome to us or
      have a material adverse affect on our business, financial position and results
      of operations or cash flows.</font></div>

      conjunction with the Consolidated Financial Statements and the Notes thereto
      presented in this Form 10-K.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong>EXECUTIVE
      OVERVIEW</strong></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">We
      began
      operations in March of 1993 as a reseller of information technology
      products.&#160;&#160;In fiscal year 1999, value-added services were added to our
      customer offerings.&#160;&#160;Value-added services represented 13.8%, 14.5% and
      14.9% of our net sales in fiscal years 2007, 2006 and 2005,
      respectively.&#160;&#160;The gross profit margins on the value-added services
      that we currently offer are significantly higher than the gross profit margins
      on our information technology product business, but require additional overhead
      expense for supervision, idle time, and other expenses related to service
      offerings that offset a portion of the increased margin.&#160; In October 2003,
      we made an initial investment in PBPO, a&#160;start up&#160;company in Tennessee
      that sells BPO services that carry&#160;higher gross profit margins, similar to
      those found in our value-added services.&#160; Then,&#160;in October 2006 we
      broadened our BPO capability by acquiring a 70% interest in Ovex, a private
      company in Pakistan that had significant experience and&#160;success in
      providing BPO services for our internal operations as well as for PBPO's
      customers.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">In
      our
      initial operating years from fiscal 1994 to fiscal 1999, with the aid of a
      robust economy and an information technology market that accommodated our
      business model, our net sales increased at a compounded annual growth rate
      of
      35.1%.&#160;&#160;Seasonal trends were never prominent in our business, although
      March quarters were historically regarded as one of the least promising
      quarters.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">In
      fiscal
      2000 we experienced our first annual net sales decline of 26%, or $173.8
      million, from net sales in fiscal 1999 due to a softer information technology
      market and difficulties in transitioning to a new enterprise resource planning
      business system. &#160;Net sales continued to decline in subsequent fiscal years
      reaching&#160;a low of $257.0 million in fiscal year 2002, or a compounded
      annual decline rate of 27% for the three years.&#160;&#160;The last five years
      have seen a compounded annual growth rate of 3.7% in net sales from $289.8
      million in fiscal year 2003 to the present $347.1 million in fiscal year
      2007.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">Net
      sales
      increased $23.4 million, or 7.2%, and gross profits increased $3.9 million,
      or
      9.8%, in fiscal year 2007 from fiscal year 2006, driven principally by increased
      product sales.&#160;&#160;Operating expenses, consisting mainly of selling and
      marketing expenses, increased a total of $3.0 million over fiscal year 2006
      results, leaving operating income of $1.1 million in fiscal year 2007, an
      improvement of $0.9 million over the $0.2 million reported in fiscal year
      2006.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">Because
      our business model involves the resale of information technology products held
      in inventory by certain distributors, we do not maintain significant amounts
      of
      inventory on hand for resale.&#160;&#160;We typically do not place an order for
      product purchases from distributors until we have received a customer purchase
      order.&#160;&#160;Inventory is then drop-shipped by the distributor to either
      the customer or shipped to our configuration center in Rancho Cucamonga,
      California.&#160;&#160;The distributor typically ships products within 24 hours
      following receipt of a purchase order and, consequently, substantially all
      of
      our product net sales in any quarter result from orders received in that
      quarter.&#160;&#160;Although we maintain a relatively small amount of inventory
      in stock for resale, most of our inventory represents either merchandise being
      configured for customers&#8217; orders or products purchased from distributors and
      shipped, but not yet received and accepted by our customers.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">Product
      revenues are generally recognized upon delivery to the
      customer.&#160;&#160;Service revenues are recognized based on contractual hourly
      rates as services are rendered or upon completion of specified contract
      services.&#160;&#160;Net sales consist of product and service revenues, less
      discounts.&#160;&#160;Cost of sales includes product and service costs and
      current and estimated allowances for returns of products that are not accepted
      by our distributors or manufacturers, less any incentive credits.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">CRITICAL
      ACCOUNTING POLICIES</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">The
      preparation of financial statements and related disclosures in conformity with
      U.S. generally accepted accounting principles and our discussion and analysis
      of
      our financial condition and results of operations require us to make judgments,
      assumptions, and estimates that affect the amounts reported in our consolidated
      financial statements and accompanying notes.&#160;&#160;Note 1 of the Notes to
      Consolidated Financial Statements of this Form 10-K describes the significant
      accounting policies and methods used in the preparation of our consolidated
      financial statements.&#160;&#160;We base our estimates on historical experience
      and on various other assumptions we believe to be reasonable under the
      circumstances, the results of which form the basis for making judgments about
      the carrying values of assets and liabilities.&#160;&#160;We regularly discuss
      with our audit committee the basis of our estimates. &#160;Actual results may
      differ from these estimates and such differences may be material.</font></div>
    <div><br></div>

    </div>
    <div><br></div>
    <div><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">We
      believe the following critical accounting policies, among others, affect our
      more significant judgments and estimates used in the preparation of our
      consolidated financial statements:</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong><em>Revenue
      recognition</em></strong>. Our net sales consist primarily of revenue from the
      sale of hardware, software, peripherals, and service and support
      contracts.&#160;&#160;We apply the provisions of the SEC Staff Accounting
      Bulletin (SAB) No. 104, &#8220;Revenue Recognition in Financial Statements,&#8221; which
      provides guidance on the recognition, presentation and disclosure of revenue
      in
      financial statements filed with the SEC.&#160;&#160;SAB No. 104 outlines the
      basic criteria that must be met to recognize revenue and provides guidance
      for
      disclosure related to revenue recognition policies.&#160;&#160;In general, we
      recognize revenue when (i) persuasive evidence of an arrangement exists, (ii)
      delivery of products has occurred or services have been rendered, (iii) the
      sales price charged is fixed or determinable and (iv) collection is reasonably
      assured.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">Under
      our
      standard shipping terms, title passes upon delivery to a common carrier but
      revenue is not recognized until delivery takes place which is generally two
      to
      three days later.&#160;&#160;Product is therefore considered received and
      accepted by the customer only upon the customer&#8217;s receipt of the product from
      the carrier.&#160;&#160;Any undelivered product is included in our
      inventory.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">The
      majority of our sales relate to physical products and are recognized on a gross
      basis with the selling price to the customer recorded as net sales and the
      acquisition cost of the product recorded as cost of sales.&#160;&#160;However,
      software maintenance contracts, software agency fees, and extended warranties
      that we sell in which we are not the primary obligor, are recorded on a net
      basis in accordance with SEC Staff Accounting Bulletin No. 104 &#8220;Revenue
      Recognition&#8221; and Emerging Issues Task Force 99-19, &#8220;Reporting Revenue Gross as a
      Principal versus Net as an Agent.&#8221; Such net revenues are recognized in full at
      the time of sale.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">We
      have
      adopted the provisions of Statement of Position No. 97-2, &#8220;Software Revenue
      Recognition&#8221; (SOP 97-2) as amended by SOP No. 98-9, &#8220;Modification of SOP 97-2,
      Software Revenue Recognition with Respect to Certain Transactions&#8221; (SOP 98-9) in
      recognizing revenue from software transactions.&#160;&#160;Revenue from software
      license sales is recognized when persuasive evidence of an arrangement exists,
      delivery of the product has been made, and a fixed fee and collectibility has
      been determined.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">Service
      revenues are recognized based on contracted hourly rates, as services are
      rendered or upon completion of specified contracted services and acceptance
      by
      the customer.&#160;&#160;Revenue from customer maintenance support
      agreements,&#160;in which we are not the primary obligor, is reported on a net
      basis and recognized at the time of the sale.&#160;Net sales consist of product
      and service revenues, less discounts and estimated allowances for sales
      returns.&#160;&#160;Cost of sales include the cost of product and services sold
      and current and estimated allowances for product returns that will not be
      accepted by our suppliers, less rebates.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">Deferred
      revenues result from prepaid management services and maintenance
      contracts.&#160;&#160;Many of our management services are pre-billed quarterly
      and income is recognized as services are performed.&#160;&#160;Our maintenance
      contracts are generally for services that may be performed over a one year
      period of time.&#160;&#160;Income is recognized on such contracts ratably over
      the period of the contract.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong><em>Allowance
      for doubtful accounts.</em></strong>&#160;We estimate our allowance for doubtful
      accounts related to trade receivables by two methods.&#160;&#160;First, we
      evaluate specific accounts over 90 days outstanding and apply various levels
      of
      risk analysis to these accounts to determine a satisfactory risk category to
      which given percentages are applied to establish a reserve.&#160;&#160;Second, a
      general reserve is established for all other accounts, exclusive of the accounts
      identified for the specific reserve, in which a percentage is applied that
      is
      supportable by historic collection patterns.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong><em>Product
      returns</em></strong><strong>.</strong>&#160; We provide an allowance for sales
      returns, which is based on historical experience.&#160;&#160;In general, we
      follow a strict policy of duplicating the terms of our vendor or manufacturers&#8217;
product return policies.&#160;&#160;However, in certain cases we must deviate
      from this policy in order to satisfy the requirements of certain sales contracts
      and/or to satisfy or maintain customer relations.&#160;&#160;To establish a
      reserve for returns, outstanding Return Merchandise Authorizations, or RMAs,
      are
      reviewed.&#160;&#160;Those RMAs issued for which the related product has not
      been returned by the customer are considered future sale reversals and are
      fully
      reserved.&#160;&#160;In addition, an estimate, based on historical return
      patterns, is provided for probable future RMAs that relate to past
      sales.&#160;&#160;Generally, customers return goods to our configuration
      facility in Rancho Cucamonga, California, where they are processed to return
      to
      the vendor.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong><em>Vendor
      returns</em></strong><strong>.</strong>&#160; After product has been returned to
      vendors under authenticated RMAs, we review such outstanding receivables from
      our vendors and establish a reserve on product that will not qualify for refund
      based on a review of specific vendor receivables.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div><br></div>

    <div><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong><em>Rebates
      and Cooperative Marketing Incentives</em></strong><strong>.</strong>&#160; We
      receive incentives from suppliers related to product and volume rebates and
      cooperative marketing development funds.&#160;&#160;These incentives are
      generally under monthly, quarterly, or annual agreements with the suppliers;
      however, some of these incentives are product driven or are provided to support
      specific programs established by the supplier.&#160;&#160;Suppliers generally
      require that we use their cooperative marketing development funds exclusively
      for advertising or other marketing programs.&#160;&#160;As marketing expenses
      are recognized, these restricted cooperative marketing development funds are
      recorded as&#160;a reduction of the related marketing expense with any excess
      funding that can not be identified with a specific vendor program reducing
      cost
      of goods sold.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">As
      rebates are earned, we record the rebate receivables with a corresponding
      reduction of cost of goods sold.&#160;&#160;Any amounts received from suppliers
      related to cooperative marketing development funds are deferred until
      earned.&#160;&#160;Incentive programs are subject to audit as to whether the
      requirements of the incentives were actually met.&#160;&#160;We establish
      reserves to cover any collectibility risks including subsequent supplier
      audits.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong><em>Inventory.</em></strong><em>&#160;&#160;</em>Although
      we employ a virtual inventory model that generally limits our exposure to
      inventory losses, with certain large customers we contractually obligate
      ourselves to product availability terms that require maintaining physical
      inventory, as well as configured product.&#160;&#160;Such inventory is generally
      confined to a very limited range of product that applies to specific customers
      or contracts.&#160;&#160;Included in our inventory is product that has been
      returned by customers but is not acceptable as returnable by the
      vendor.&#160;&#160;As a result, we expose ourselves to losses from such
      inventory that requires reserves for losses to be established.&#160;&#160;We
      record varying reserves based upon the class of inventory (i.e. held for resale
      or returned from customers) and age of inventory.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong>RESULTS
      OF OPERATIONS</strong></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">The
      following table sets forth certain financial data as a percentage of net sales
      for the periods indicated.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong>COMPARISON
      OF FISCAL YEARS ENDED SEPTEMBER 30, 2007 AND 2006</strong></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong>NET
      SALES.&#160;&#160; </strong>Net sales increased $23.4 million, or 7.2%, to
      $347.1 million in fiscal year 2007 from $323.7 million in fiscal year
      2006.&#160;&#160;Our affiliate, PBPO, and subsidiary, Ovex, contributed $3.2
      million and $0.9 million, respectively, of the total net sales increase with
      the
      remaining $19.3 million increase coming from our core operations of sales and
      service of information technology products.&#160;&#160;While no one customer
      accounted for 10% or more of total net sales in fiscal years 2007 or 2006,
      the
      core operation increase in sales resulted, in fact, from large volume customers
      who purchased increased amounts of our products and
      services.&#160;&#160;&#160;For example, net sales to our top five customers
      accounted for 39.6% of total net sales in fiscal year 2007.&#160;&#160;Net sales
      to these top five customers increased $53.1 million, or 15.6%, in fiscal year
      2007 over the total net sales to these same five customers in the prior fiscal
      year.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">Product
      net sales in fiscal year 2007 increased $22.6 million, or 8.2%, over fiscal
      year
      2006 and were responsible for most of the increase in the total net sales for
      the year.&#160;&#160;Top selling products were software, desktop computers and
      laptops, respectively, for both fiscal years 2007 and 2006 with software sales
      being the leading component of the sales mix.&#160;&#160;Software agency
      commissions, a part of product sales, increased for the third consecutive year
      in fiscal year 2007, to $7.0 million, an increase of $1.5 million, or 21.0%
      over
      fiscal 2006 commissions.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">Service
      net sales in fiscal year 2007 increased a marginal $0.8 million, or 1.7% over
      fiscal year 2006.&#160;&#160;Service net sales from our affiliate, PBPO, and our
      subsidiary, Ovex, that promotes and performs business process outsourcing
      services, increased $4.1 million to an aggregate of $6.7 million for fiscal
      year
      2007 and were responsible for all of the increase in our service net sales
      for
      fiscal year 2007.&#160;&#160;Core service net sales in fiscal year 2007, which
      relate to the service of information technology products and exclude the
      contributions of PBPO and Ovex, decreased $3.3 million to $41.1 million from
      $44.4 million in fiscal year 2006.&#160;&#160;The decline in core service net
      sales in fiscal year 2007 was in large part from the conclusion of a substantial
      municipal services work project that was principally completed in fiscal year
      2006 as well as from a decrease of services to a major customer that has been
      adversely affected by the general slow down in the mortgage
      industry.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong>GROSS
      PROFIT.&#160; </strong>Gross profits increased $3.9 million, or 9.8%, to $43.6
      million in fiscal year 2007 from $39.7 million for fiscal year
      2006.&#160;&#160;The bulk of the increase in gross profits, $2.2 million, was
      from product gross profits, with the remainder $1.7 million attributable to
      services.&#160; Our affiliate, PBPO, and subsidiary, Ovex, contributed
      approximately one-third of the gross profits increase, or $1.3 million, on
      aggregate base sales of $2.1 million for fiscal year 2007.&#160;&#160;Overall
      gross margins improved to 12.5% in fiscal year 2007 from 12.2% in the prior
      fiscal year.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">Product
      gross profits increased $2.2 million in fiscal year 2007 to $25.2 million from
      $23.0 million in the prior fiscal year principally from increased sales
      volume.&#160;&#160;Product gross margin percentages improved marginally to 8.4%
      in fiscal year 2007 from 8.3% in fiscal year 2006.&#160;&#160;The slight
      improvement in margins was attributable to the increase in agency commission
      fees that bear no associated costs.&#160; Excluding the agency commissions,
      product gross margins fell to 6.1% in fiscal year 2007 from 6.3% in the prior
      fiscal year.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">Service
      gross profits increased $1.7 million in fiscal year 2007 to $18.3 million from
      $16.6 million in the prior fiscal year.&#160;&#160;Most of the increase, $1.1
      million, was attributable to an increase in service gross profits from our
      affiliate, PBPO, which operates on an approximate 35% service gross
      margin.&#160;&#160;Our core service gross profits, which relates to the service
      of information technology products and excludes the contributions of PBPO and
      Ovex, increased marginally $0.4 million in fiscal year 2007 to $16.2 million
      from $15.8 million in the prior fiscal year.&#160;&#160;Related core service
      gross margins increased 3.8% to 39.4% from 35.6%.</font></div>
    <div><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">While
      core service net sales were down, core service gross profits and margins were
      up.&#160;&#160;Most of the service gross margin improvement can be traced to a
      major municipal service project that was largely completed in fiscal year 2006
      and whose revenues of $4.2 million and service gross margins of 11% adversely
      impacted fiscal 2006 results causing a 3% drop in overall gross margins for
      that
      year.</font></div>
    <div><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt;"><strong>SELLING
      AND MARKETING
      EXPENSES.</strong></font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt;">&#160;
Selling and
      marketing expenses increased $2.2 million, or 7.9%, to $30.5 million
      in fiscal year 2007, from $28.3 million in fiscal year 2006.&#160;&#160;The $2.2
      million increase in selling and marketing expenses in fiscal year 2007 was
      attributable principally to a $1.9 million increase in wages from the hiring
      of
      an additional 48 employees, including 40 for the call center&#160;in the
</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt;">U.S.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt;">
      and 8 for the recently formed cabling
      division, and $0.2 million in increased overtime pay.&#160;&#160;The remaining
      $0.1 increase in selling and marketing expenses relates to increases in expenses
      for our affiliate, PBPO, and subsidiary, Ovex.&#160;&#160;Selling and marketing
      expenses expressed as a percentage of net sales, were flat at 8.8% for fiscal
      years 2007 and 2006.</font></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong>GENERAL
      AND ADMINISTRATIVE EXPENSES.</strong>&#160; General and administrative expenses,
      or G&amp;A, increased $0.8 million, or 7.0%, to $11.9 million in fiscal year
      2007 from $11.1 in fiscal year 2006.&#160;&#160;All of the increase was
      attributed to our affiliate, PBPO, and subsidiary, Ovex, with G&amp;A expense
      for PBPO and Ovex increasing $0.4 million and $0.6 million
      respectively.&#160;&#160;The Ovex increase was due to our acquisition of Ovex
      stock and Ovex&#8217;s merger in fiscal year 2007 with no comparable expense in prior
      fiscal years.&#160; The majority of the increase for PBPO relates to increases
      in salary as well as increases in travel and entertainment related
      costs.&#160;&#160;As with selling and marketing expenses, when G&amp;A expenses
      are expressed as a percentage of net sales, the results are flat at 3.4% for
      fiscal years 2007 and 2006.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong>OPERATING
      INCOME.</strong>&#160; Operating income increased $0.9 million in fiscal year
      2007&#160;to $1.1 million as compared with $0.2 million in the prior fiscal
      year.&#160;&#160;The increase of $0.9 million in operating income can be
      attributed to the increase in gross profit of $3.9 million less the $3.0 million
      increase in operating expenses during fiscal year 2007 as discussed
      above.</font></div>
    <div><br></div>

            <td valign="bottom" width="9%" bgcolor="#cceeff" style="BORDER-BOTTOM: black 3pt double">

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">Net
      interest income increased $0.1 million in fiscal year 2007&#160;to $0.3 million
      from $0.2 million in fiscal year 2006.&#160;&#160;Interest income in both fiscal
      years resulted from our short term cash investments.&#160;&#160;&#160;Interest
      expense increased $0.2 million in fiscal year 2007 to $0.3 million from $0.1
      million in fiscal year 2006.&#160; The increase was principally from the
      acquisition of Ovex in fiscal year 2007 and the related interest expense that
      was not present in the prior fiscal year.&#160; The&#160;Ovex interest expense
      includes $0.1 million related to short-term borrowings under an export finance
      program.&#160;&#160;In addition, consolidated interest expense includes
      approximately $0.1 million related to capitalized leases.&#160; The interest
      expense in fiscal years 2007 and 2006 from our lending facility with GE
      Commercial Distribution Finance Corporation was approximately $11,000 and
      $14,000 respectively, which is customarily low&#160;due to our interest-free
      borrowing periods allowed under the financing.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">&#160;&#160;</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong>OTHER
      INCOME.</strong>&#160;&#160;Other income increased a marginal $43,000 in fiscal
      year 2007 as compared with fiscal year 2006 but was not a significant factor
      for
      either fiscal year.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong>INCOME
      TAX (BENEFIT) PROVISION</strong>.&#160;&#160;A $203,000 tax benefit was provided
      for fiscal year 2007, which arose principally from&#160;a $400,000 decrease to
      our valuation allowance for deferred tax benefits related to&#160;net operating
      loss tax benefits.&#160; The decrease of $400,000 represented our estimate of
      the federal and state taxes at a combined rate of 40% that would be incurred
      in
      future periods and for which the tax benefit of the deferred net operating
      loss
      deduction would be available.&#160; Only $263,000 of the $400,000 decrease was
      available for the reduction of deferred taxes&#160;since the balance, $137,000,
      relates to net operating losses arising from stock options and are considered
      an
      adjustment of equity.&#160; As a result of the use of the deferred net operating
      loss of $263,000, future provisions&#160;for taxes, for financial statement
      purposes, will not benefit from the net operating loss deduction and will be
      computed at&#160;the full statutory&#160;rates.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">We
      file a
      consolidated federal income tax return, while for many of our state tax returns
      we file separately under the name of our wholly-owned sales subsidiary, En
      Pointe Technologies Sales, Inc., that is qualified to do business in all fifty
      states.&#160;&#160;Our consolidated return excludes both PBPO and Ovex because
      in the case of PBPO, our investment is less than the required 80% to consolidate
      under &#160;federal tax law.&#160;&#160;In the case of Ovex, we are not taxed on
      foreign income until it is distributed.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">As
      of
      September 30, 2007 we had $5.3 million of&#160; federal NOL carry-forwards,
      which at 35% federal tax rates would reduce future federal taxes by $1.9
      million.&#160; In addition, there are $0.1 million&#160;of alternative minimum
      tax credits carry-forwards that bring the total future benefit to $2.0 million,
      of which $0.4 million was recognized in fiscal year 2007.&#160;&#160;The NOL
      carry-forwards are scheduled to expire at various dates through fiscal year
      2023. &#160;Section 382 of the Internal Revenue Code could&#160;limit the future
      use of some or all of the NOL carry-forwards if the ownership of our common
      stock changes by more than 50 percentage points in certain circumstances over
      a
      three year testing period.&#160;&#160;</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong>MINORITY
      INTEREST.</strong>&#160; Under FIN 46 and other recent changes in consolidation
      principles, certain minority interests are required to be
      consolidated.&#160;&#160;We own an approximate 30% voting interest in PBPO and
      under FIN 46 are required to consolidate PBPO&#8217;s financial results in our
      financial statements.&#160;&#160;As a result, we allocate certain losses to the
      other stockholders of PBPO who collectively own approximately 70% of
      PBPO.&#160;Losses so allocated to the &#8220;minority interest&#8221; are not based upon the
      percentage of ownership, but upon the &#8220;at risk&#8221; capital of those owners.
&#160;Once the &#8220;minority interest at risk&#8221; capital has been absorbed by losses,
      all remaining losses are allocated to us, without regard for the amount of
      capital that we hold &#8220;at risk&#8221;.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong>NET
      INCOME</strong>.&#160;&#160;Net income increased $1.1 million to $1.6 million in
      fiscal year 2007 from $0.5 million in fiscal year 2006.&#160;&#160;The principal
      reasons for the $1.1 million increase in net income was from the $0.9 million
      increase in operating income and the $0.2 million decrease in income
      taxes.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong>COMPARISON
      OF FISCAL YEARS ENDED SEPTEMBER 30, 2006 AND 2005</strong></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong>NET
      SALES</strong>.&#160;&#160;Net sales decreased $4.6 million, or 1.4%, to $323.7
      million in fiscal year 2006 from $328.3 million in fiscal year
      2005.&#160;&#160;Moderating the net sales decrease was the business of Software
      Medium, Inc., that we acquired in January 2006 and that contributed $3.9 million
      in net sales for fiscal year 2006 and PBPO, our variable interest entity
      affiliate, whose sales increased $1.7 million.&#160;&#160;No one customer
      accounted for 10% or more of total net sales in fiscal year 2006 or
      2005.&#160;&#160;However, sales do tend to be concentrated in a relatively few
      accounts as evidenced in fiscal years 2006 and 2005 when our top five customers
      made up 27.1% and 31.9%, respectively, of total net sales and our top
      twenty-five customers contributed 59.7% and 63.4%, respectively, of total net
      sales.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">On
      a
      quarterly seasonal basis, our June quarter, helped by software agency
      commissions of $1.1 million, was the strongest net sales quarter of the fiscal
      year for the third consecutive year with the June 2006 fiscal quarter coming
      in
      at $95.6 million compared with $92.6 million in prior fiscal year
      period.&#160;&#160;On the other hand, the March quarter of fiscal 2006 continued
      to be the weakest net sales quarter of the fiscal year for the third consecutive
      year.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">Product
      sales in fiscal year 2006 decreased $2.6 million, or 0.9%, to $276.7 million
      from $279.3 million reported in fiscal year 2005, reflecting a decline in
      overall net sales from a few of our major customers.&#160;&#160;Service revenues
      in fiscal year 2006 decreased year-over-year $2.0 million, a lesser decline
      than
      reported in product sales, but at a higher rate of 4.1%, to $47.0 million from
      the $49.0 million reported in the prior fiscal year.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong>GROSS
      PROFIT.</strong>&#160; Gross profits increased $4.6 million, or 13.1%, to $39.7
      million in fiscal year 2006 from $35.1 million for fiscal year 2005. Services
      contributed $2.5 million of the gross profits increase, with products
      responsible for remaining $2.1 million.&#160;&#160;With declining net sales, the
      increase in gross profits came solely from improvements in gross margin
      percentages which improved for both product and services to a combined 12.2%
      from 10.7% in fiscal year 2005.&#160;&#160;Product gross margin percentages
      improved by 0.9% to 8.3% in fiscal year 2006 while service improved by 6.4%
      to
      35.5%.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">Most
      of
      the $2.1 million increase in product gross profits came from agency commission
      fees of $1.8 million which in turn originated primarily from increased Microsoft
      software commission fees.&#160;&#160;The service gross profits increase of $2.5
      million was from a combination of factors, however. PBPO, our consolidated
      affiliate, contributed $0.8 million of the increase in service gross profits
      for
      fiscal year 2006 over fiscal year 2005.&#160;&#160;Two large logistic and asset
      management customers contributed the majority of the remaining $1.7 million
      increase in service gross profits.&#160;&#160;These were high volume projects in
      which processing costs were successfully contained.&#160;&#160;Other factors
      explaining the increase include the reaching of certain contractual milestones
      with our municipal service contracts that allowed us to recognize higher service
      margins as well as our acquisition in January 2006 of a security services
      business that traditionally earns above average gross profit
      margins.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong>SELLING
      AND MARKETING EXPENSES.</strong>&#160; Selling and marketing expenses increased
      $2.5 million, or 9.9%, to $28.3 million in fiscal year 2006, from $25.8 million
      in fiscal year 2005.&#160;&#160;The $2.5 million increase is inclusive of a
      decrease in PBPO&#8217;s selling and marketing expenses of $0.3
      million.&#160;&#160;Excluding the decrease in PBPO&#8217;s selling and marketing
      expense, our core selling and marketing expenses increased by $2.8
      million.&#160;&#160;The increase in selling and marketing expenses in fiscal
      year 2006 resulted primarily from $2.7 million of wage related expenses
      consisting of $1.4 million in commissions, mainly from increased software sales
      and draws, $0.9 million in wages, and $0.4 million in employee benefits and
      reimbursements.</font></div>

      also
      experienced a $0.8 million increase in our business process outsourcing expenses
      from increased use of employees offshore and from costs related to software
      programming in India.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">However,

      and
      from a favorable settlement of disputed balances with creditors.&#160;When
      selling and marketing expenses are expressed as a percentage of net sales,
      there
      was an increase of 0.9% to 8.8% in fiscal year 2006 from 7.9% in fiscal year
      2005.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong>GENERAL
      AND ADMINISTRATIVE EXPENSES.</strong>&#160; General and administrative expenses,
      or G&amp;A, increased $1.0 million, or 9.4%, to $11.1 million in fiscal year
      2006 from $10.1 in fiscal year 2005.&#160;&#160;The increase in G&amp;A was
      principally the result of higher legal expenses of $0.7 million due to the
      three
      legal suits that we defended and to $0.3 million in the settlement of the First
      Union securities matter dating back to 2000.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">When
      G&amp;A expenses are expressed as a percentage of net sales, there was an
      increase of 0.3% to 3.4% in fiscal year 2006 from 3.1% in fiscal year
      2005.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong>OPERATING
      INCOME (LOSS).</strong>&#160; Operating income of $0.2 million was realized in
      fiscal year 2006 compared with $0.9 million of operating loss in the prior
      fiscal year.&#160;&#160;The increase of $1.1 million in operating income can be
      attributed to the increase in gross profit of $4.6 million less the $3.5 million
      increase in operating expenses during fiscal year 2006 as discussed
      above.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong>INTEREST
      (INCOME) EXPENSE, NET.</strong>&#160; Interest income of $0.2 million in fiscal
      year 2006 is net of interest expense of $0.1 million. &#160;Interest income
      resulted from our short term cash investments while most of interest expense
      in
      fiscal year 2006 was related to capitalized leases for computer equipment
      acquired.&#160;&#160;The interest expense in fiscal year 2006 from our lending
      facility with GE Commercial Distribution Finance Corporation was approximately
      $14,000 which is customarily low or non-existent due to our interest-free
      borrowing periods allowed under the financing.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">Net
      interest income increased $0.2 million in fiscal year 2006 compared with the
      prior fiscal year.&#160;&#160;Most of the increase can be attributed to the
      inclusion in fiscal year 2005 of $0.2 million of interest expense related to
      the
      Ontario configuration facility that was not present in the fiscal year 2006
      due
      to the Ontario lease converting from a financing lease to an operating lease
      in
      which rentexpense replaces interest expense as a major expense
      item.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong>OTHER
      INCOME.</strong>&#160; Other income decreased $0.6 million in fiscal year 2006
      from that of fiscal year 2005.&#160;&#160;The decrease in other income was due
      to the inclusion in fiscal year 2005 of insurance recovery from prior year
      losses and rental income which did not repeat in fiscal year 2006.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;"><strong>PROVISION
      FOR INCOME TAXES.</strong>&#160; We provided a $42,000 tax provision for fiscal
      year 2006, an increase of $21,000 from that provided in the prior fiscal
      year.&#160;&#160;While we are not subject to the regular 34% corporate federal
      income tax rates because of the tax benefit derived from our past net operating
      losses, or NOLs, that can be carried forward, we are nevertheless subject to
      the
      federal alternative minimum tax.&#160;&#160;The alternative minimum tax limits
      NOL carryforwards that can be applied in any one year to 90% of the current
      year&#8217;s taxable income and imposes a 20% tax on the remaining 10% of taxable
      income.&#160;</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">We
      file a
      consolidated federal income tax return, while for many of our state tax returns
      we file separately under the name of our wholly-owned sales subsidiary, En
      Pointe Technologies Sales, Inc., that is qualified to do business in all fifty
      states.&#160;&#160;Our consolidated return excludes PBPO because our investment
      is less than the required 80% to consolidate under federal tax
      law.&#160;&#160;Thus, none of the losses generated by PBPO are available for the
      reduction of income taxes.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.7pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman;">As
      of
      September 30, 2006 we had $6.9 million of NOL carry-forwards for which a 100%
      valuation allowance has been provided.&#160;&#160;The NOL carry-forwards are
      scheduled to expire at various dates through fiscal year
      2023.&#160;&#160;Section 382 of the Internal Revenue Code could limit the future
      use of some or all of the NOL carry-forwards if the ownership of our common
      stock changes by more than 50 percentage points in certain circumstances over
      a
      three year testing period.&#160;&#160;Of the $6.9 million NOL carry-forwards,
      $4.7 million will be considered an adjustment to additional paid-in capital
      and
      will not benefit future earnings, since those losses were attributable to the
      exercise of employee stock options, which had been recognized as expense for
      tax
      purposes but not for financial statement purposes.</font></div>
